dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (Japan Medical Association open-source receipt system), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Program SOKATU0210 handles national health insurance monthly claim aggregation.
evidence: Project code name ORCA in header comment
COPY directives referencing ORCA-specific copybooks (CPORCSPRTLNK.INC, COMMON-SPA, CPPTINF.INC)
No COMP-3 usage, no EXEC CICS/SQL
File assigns use environment variable names (SKT0210TP, RECEUPD, RECEERR) typical of GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL runtime

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese national health insurance (Kokuho) monthly claim (Seikyusho) aggregation processing for the JMA ORCA medical receipt system
purpose.summary: SOKATU0210 is a batch program in the JMA ORCA medical receipt system that aggregates monthly insurance claim data (Seikyusho) for national health insurance (Kokuho). It reads a temporary claim file, processes patient and insured-person records, and writes updated claim DB records and error files. The program handles special cases such as elderly patients, maternity, and public expense billing categories.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY directives (33 copybooks) for JMA ORCA shared layouts
61 CALL statements indicating modular subprogram architecture
ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED with DYNAMIC access for temporary claim file
ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL for update/error output files
Japanese EUC-JP encoded comments (decoded as latin-1 garbled)
Detailed revision history spanning 2005-2017 with named authors
REDEFINES usage for hospital name/address fields
OCCURS tables for public expense number aggregation (WRK-2007-TBL)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — flat-file based processing
Program option support added in 2014 revision
verdict.notes: Source file is encoded in EUC-JP (Japanese); decoded as latin-1 causing garbled comment text. All Japanese comments are readable in context as EUC-JP. File is truncated at 16000 chars out of 130323 bytes (2937 lines total). The program is clearly production-grade JMA ORCA software with a long maintenance history (2005-2017).
